analytical_models.equation_role: Predict equilibrium fractions of ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide (κ) versus temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Calculated that ferrite forms first during solidification, followed by austenite by peritectic reaction.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel; equilibrium phase fractions of ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide calculated for temperatures above 550 °C.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated phase fractions show the general trend similar to the XRD-measured volume fractions; the calculated κ-carbide dissolution temperature (about 823 °C) is lower than the experimental dissolution temperature (between 850 and 900 °C). Differences attributed to non-equilibrium state and to calculated atomic fraction vs measured volume fraction.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: κ-carbide is harder to deform than α and γ and acts as an obstacle for deformation; microcracks are easier to initiate around κ-carbide, decreasing ductility.

interfaces.interface_notes: κ-carbide is present mainly at α/γ boundaries, along α/α boundaries in large α areas, and dispersed in the γ phase area.
interfaces.phase_evolution: On annealing at 800 °C the γ fraction rises to about 29% while α and κ-carbide fractions decrease relative to the 700 °C condition; the κ-carbide coarsens and adopts a globular shape, and the prior γ→α+κ eutectoid lamellar N–W orientation relationship (seen at 700 °C) is largely lost, so no orientation relationship is found between κ-carbide and α.

phase_interfaces.coherence: incoherent — no orientation relationship found between κ-carbide and its neighboring α phase in the 800 °C specimen

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 20 kg ingot of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel was prepared by vacuum induction melting.
Ingot heated to 1200 °C then forged to a forging blank.
Forging blank homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h before hot rolling.
Homogenized blank hot-rolled to a 3 mm thick plate with finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C.
After rolling the plate was water quenched to about 300 °C.
Air cooled stage of the hot-rolling schedule shown in Fig. 1.
Hot-rolled plate annealed at 800 °C for 1 h.

structures.overall_structure: Banded α + γ + κ-carbide microstructure. Ferrite (α) ferrite bands/large α areas, austenite (γ) areas, and κ-carbide distributed mainly between α and γ areas or along α/α boundaries in large α areas, with some κ-carbide dispersed in the γ phase area.

unmapped_findings: The κ-carbide dissolution temperature is between 850 °C and 900 °C (higher than the 823 °C calculated by Thermo-Calc); in the 800 °C specimen κ-carbide is still present and detectable by XRD (κ reflections present only in the 700, 800 and 850 °C specimens).

Fracture of the 800 °C specimen occurs by a mixture mode of ductile fracture and quasi-cleavage fracture: the dimpled area is mainly produced by ductile transgranular fracture of γ and the river pattern mainly by quasi-cleavage of α phase; κ-carbide distributed in the matrix and along grain boundaries contributes to cleavage fracture from grain boundaries (large secondary cracks related to the banded microstructure).

The lattice of α phase changes in the range 2.89–2.91 Å, of γ phase in 3.65–3.67 Å, and of κ-carbide in 3.76–3.79 Å; the lattice expansion of α and γ phases contributes to the low density of the steel (6.80 g/cm3, about 13% lower than pure Fe).
No obvious TRIP or TWIP phenomenon is found during the tensile test (based on TEM examination of the deformed microstructure).

Ordering of atoms in α phase or γ phase is not expected during annealing at 700–1200 °C for 1 h (no obvious superlattice spots in SADPs), though ordering may occur during quenching but the time is too short for it to develop well.

For the specimen annealed at 800 °C, the work hardening rate is in the reverse order of annealing temperature relative to the other specimens when true strain is less than about 5% (higher than the ≥900 °C specimens, which contain no obvious κ-carbide in the matrix), but it decreases quickly until failure occurs.
